newsitem.title: DENMARK: Bank shares still in focus on Danish stock market.
newsitem.headline: Bank shares still in focus on Danish stock market.

text.p: Danish share prices ended Monday up from Friday's close but well off early highs and dealers said that their progress on Tuesday depended on the evening's trade on Wall Street.
"Among the most popular shares today were the big banks and one would also expect them to influence trade tomorrow," a dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index gained 0.17 point to 121.72 in bourse turnover of 806 million crowns and its September future, which expires on September 20, rose 0.10 point to 121.60 with 1,791 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Most traded paper of the day was Dan Danske Bank, rising 3.94 crowns to 435.94 with some 230,000 shares changing hands.
Unidanmark rose two crowns to 279 but third-largest bank BG Bank was untraded at 228 crowns.
Tele Danmark slipped three crowns to 278 crowns after Goldman Sachs downgraded its recommendation to 'perform', from 'outperform'. It was also weakening in early trade on the New York exchange.
SAS fell 1.5 crowns to 63 crowns. It faces new competitors and a potential price war on some routes.
